This application has been filed with a prayer to release the accused applicant on bail in Case Crime No.335 of 2022, under Sections 363, 376, 504, 506 I.P.C. & 3/4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act and 64(a) The Information Technology (Amendment) Act, 2008, Police Station Kotwali, District Shahjahanpur.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Heard Mr. Jai Prakash Singh, learned counsel for the accused applicant, Ms. Beena Mishra, learned counsel for the informant and Mr. Rajesh Kumar Sachan, learned Brief Holder for the State respondent.
Learned counsel for the accused applicant has submitted that the accused applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the crime.
He further submitted that the victim had love affairs with the accused applicant and she willingly went with him but

entities.text: Sanjeev Alias Sandeep Alias Chiku vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the applicant should be released on bail.

Learned Brief Holder appearing on behalf of the State has opposed the bail application of the accused applicant and submitted that the victim is a minor girl, aged about 15 years and her consent being minor, has no meaning in the eyes of law.
Therefore, the accused applicant should not be enlarged on bail.
Considered the rival submissions made by the parties' counsel and perused the material available on record.
It transpires from the record that the victim has supported the version of the F.I.R. in her statements recorded under Sections 161 & 164 of Cr.P.C.
She is a minor girl aged about 15 years and her consent being minor has no meaning in the eyes of law.
Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case as mentioned above, nature of the crime and severity of punishment, it does not appear just to enlarge the applicant on bail.
The prayer for bail is declined and the bail application of applicant- Sanjeev Alias Sandeep Alias Chiku is rejected.
